title: Export holds every part the search matches, even rows not yet loaded
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create 35 active parts for this test whose part numbers start with the same text, so one search lists all 35.
  • Have another active part, part A, whose part number does not start with that text.
  • Use a computer that can open the exported file in a spreadsheet program.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Search box.
  2. Do not scroll the list.
  3. Click the three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar, to the left of New Inventory Part.
  4. Click Export.
  5. Open the downloaded file.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The 35 parts are listed (the list loads 30 rows until you scroll).

Step 2:

  • The list stays at its first rows.

Step 3:

  • The menu opens.

Step 4:

  • A file downloads.

Step 5:

  • The file holds 35 part rows, one for each part the search matches, so it also holds the 5 rows not yet loaded (35 − 30 = 5).
  • Part A is not in the file, because the search does not match it.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10814 (Story 1, Active and Inactive Tabs on the Inventory List), story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk)

  • S1-R9b: “The export includes every part on that tab that matches the current search, filters and Supply filter, including parts not yet scrolled into view. With nothing matching, the message "Empty export" shows and no file is made.”
  • S1-R9: “Export in the actions menu exports the parts on the tab that shows: active parts from the Active tab, inactive parts from the Inactive tab.”
  • S2-R6: “The checkbox in the header ticks or clears every row loaded in the list. The list loads 30 parts at a time as the user scrolls, so it ticks only the rows loaded so far. The count in the bar shows exactly how many parts will change.”
